c.tagline: A fairy-tale city of spires and bridges.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Old Town, Charles Bridge and tram 22; taxi, currency-exchange and strip-club scams in the centre

hood_desc: The medieval core around the Astronomical Clock and the Old Town Square, all cobbled lanes, Gothic spires and crowds. Ideal for first-timers who want to be steps from the city's iconic sights, though it is busy and touristy.
The picturesque Lesser Town below Prague Castle, full of baroque palaces, gardens, winding streets and the Charles Bridge approach. Perfect for romantics who want fairytale charm and postcard views.
A grander, more open district built around Wenceslas Square, mixing shopping, hotels, theaters and nightlife. Suits visitors wanting a central, bustling base with commerce and easy transport.
A leafy, upscale residential neighborhood of handsome apartment buildings, parks, wine bars and stylish cafes. Great for those seeking a local, relaxed feel and a strong food and drink scene.

A gritty, bohemian district famous for having the most pubs per capita, plus the towering TV Tower and a lively, alternative nightlife. Best for budget travelers and night owls chasing an authentic, unpolished vibe.

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Buy tickets via the PID Litacka app, station machines, or a rechargeable Litacka card from DPP info centers; contactless bank-card tap-in is also accepted network-wide. A 30-minute ticket costs 36-39 CZK (~$1.60) and a 24-hour pass 140-150 CZK (~$6.20).
transit.hours: Metro runs about 5am-midnight; night trams and buses run all night at reduced frequency.
